en: The Philippines consists of exactly 7,641 islands, an increase from the previously recorded count of 7,107 islands.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer long underground river that flows directly through a cave into the sea.
The Philippine Sea covers an estimated area of 5 million square kilometers, making it larger than the combined land area of the Philippines and Japan.
The San Juanico Bridge spans 2.16 kilometers across the San Juanico Strait, physically connecting the islands of Leyte and Samar.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon, forming the longest range in the country.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of about 4,000 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the Philippines.
The Philippine Tarsier measures only 85 to 160 millimeters in body length, making it one of the smallest primates in the world.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering approximately 14,649 square kilometers across its main island and smaller islets.
Aliwagwag Falls in Davao Oriental features a series of cascades dropping a total of 340 meters, making it one of the highest waterfalls in the country.
